executiveSummary: Law enforcement unsealed a major case alleging approximately $129 million in losses from AI-enabled executive and attorney impersonation that tricked employees into wiring funds; the case spans multiple sectors and countries and underscores business email compromise convergence with deepfake voice and video. View Article Source U.S. election stakeholders face elevated risk from deepfake audio/video combined with phishing and smishing, according to a federal public service announcement and subsequent reporting. Security Advisory Separately, researchers tracked widespread election misinformation with AI-generated campaign imagery circulating across platforms. Supporting Report In Europe, an EU-assessed network linked to Russia reportedly used cloned voices, fabricated news videos, and manipulated images to inflame unrest in France, adding to concern over state-aligned information operations. View Article Defensively, OpenAI reported disrupting false-front influence operations that planted articles, fake documents, and scripted audio, while new provenance tools and standards continue to roll out; however, recent studies show speech watermarking and image deepfake detectors can be evaded, highlighting an active detection arms race. Source Research Research A convicted fraudster's use of generative AI to forge corporate takeover documents in the UK illustrates legal and market-manipulation risks from AI-authored paperwork and synthetic identities. View Article Overall, the threat environment appears to be worsening due to concurrent high-impact financial fraud, election-targeted deception, and sophisticated influence operations.

Implement out-of-band verification for any financial or access-changing request conveyed via voice/video or urgent messaging. Mark high-risk workflows with mandatory callbacks to known numbers. (Analyst Recommendation)

Deploy layered authenticity checks: cryptographic content credentials (C2PA), robust logging of capture/edit chains, and multi-detector ensembles with human review for high-stakes media. (Analyst Recommendation)

For elections and public-sector comms, pre-establish official channels and publish verification procedures for donors, volunteers, and vendors; rehearse incident-response for synthetic-media events. (Analyst Recommendation)
Newsrooms should gate inbound materials with provenance verification at intake; preserve headers, EXIF/C2PA, and maintain a ledger of suspicious submitters. (Analyst Recommendation)
Finance and treasury teams should require dual authorization and time delays for non-routine transfers; log and audit any approval by audio/video meeting. (Analyst Recommendation)
Law enforcement and public agencies should publish clear guidance that fines/warrants are never settled via phone and provide a hotline for verification. (Analyst Recommendation)
